blockers_fixed.root_cause: Desktop treated account-service HTTP denials as offline and fell back to cached account/license state; local workflow routes lacked server-side account/license enforcement.
blockers_fixed.fix: HTTP 401/403 license/profile responses now clear cached credentials and return invalid account state; protected workflow routes now require an authenticated active license.
blockers_fixed.before: Service denied the banned user, but Desktop still reported authenticated and protected routes returned 200.
blockers_fixed.after: Desktop reports unauthenticated, clears tokens, and protected routes return 403.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: Local account recovery still depends on the service refusing blocked users; service remains authoritative.

blockers_fixed.root_cause: Desktop cached auth/license fallback was used after service 403.
blockers_fixed.fix: Server-denied account/license checks no longer enter offline grace; credentials are cleared on 401/403.
blockers_fixed.before: Suspended user was denied by service but remained authenticated in Desktop.
blockers_fixed.after: Suspended user becomes unauthenticated in Desktop and cached tokens are removed.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: None beyond normal local-machine compromise assumptions.

blockers_fixed.root_cause: Desktop workflow dispatch directly invoked local APIs without account/license checks.
blockers_fixed.fix: Added account/license gate to protected workflow routes in both dispatch and optional FastAPI paths.
blockers_fixed.before: Expired license returned invalid from license check but local workflow route returned 200.
blockers_fixed.after: Expired license receives 403 license_required on protected workflows.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: Older unauthenticated desktop workflow tests are obsolete for account-gated routes.

blockers_fixed.attack: device revocation use from revoked device
blockers_fixed.root_cause: Access JWTs were not bound to active session/device records; device revocation only blocked refresh.
blockers_fixed.fix: Issued access tokens now include session_id and device_id; protected dependencies verify active unrevoked session and active device on every request.
blockers_fixed.before: Revoked device could still use old access token against /user/me.
blockers_fixed.after: Old access token is rejected after device/session revocation.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: Pre-186E tokens without session/device claims require re-login.

blockers_fixed.attack: device limit bypass and fake device ids
blockers_fixed.root_cause: Existing device_id lookup did not verify ownership before reuse.
blockers_fixed.fix: Existing device IDs are rejected unless owned by the authenticating user.
blockers_fixed.before: Another account could reuse an existing device_id and create a session.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: Device IDs remain client-generated but are ownership-checked server-side.

blockers_fixed.root_cause: event_type was a whitelisted string field but not constrained to known values.
blockers_fixed.fix: event_type is now validated against an allow-list; secret regex catches GitHub, Anthropic-style, JWT-looking, and path-like values.
blockers_fixed.before: ghp-style secret and code-shaped event_type strings returned 204.
blockers_fixed.after: Unknown/secret/code-shaped event_type values return 422; valid heartbeat returns 204.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: New analytics events require explicit allow-list changes.

blockers_fixed.attack: offline grace extension by editing local cache
blockers_fixed.root_cause: Desktop trusted unsigned local token expiry and license_checked_at cache values.
blockers_fixed.fix: Desktop account cache now has an HMAC integrity marker over sensitive auth/license fields; tampered state returns local_state_tampered and does not authenticate.
blockers_fixed.before: Editing local timestamps extended offline grace and restored authenticated valid state.
blockers_fixed.after: Edited cache fails integrity and returns unauthenticated invalid state.
blockers_fixed.residual_risk: A user with write access to both cache and local signing secret can replace local state; online service checks remain authoritative.

residual_risks: Local cache HMAC blocks direct timestamp/token edits, but a user with write access to both the cache and its local signing secret can replace local state; online account service checks remain authoritative.
Pre-186E access tokens without session_id/device_id claims are rejected and require re-login after update.
Refresh replay is rejected; broader session-family invalidation remains unchanged from Phase 186D info findings and was not a confirmed blocker.
